title: Violet’s Keepsakes
sub: Grades 1–2 · Violet’s Life · A life in order
objective: Children will follow the life of Violet Dina Want, a working woman born in London in 1907, through the keepsakes of the *Violet’s Life* room: a house, a sewing machine, wedding rings, a coat and a rose. They will put her life in order, say what a keepsake or a photograph tells us about a person, and think of a question to ask a woman in their own family.

objectives.heading: By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
objectives.why: Women’s History Month remembers famous women, and everyday women too. Every family has a woman whose story is worth keeping.

items.text: tell three parts of Violet’s life in order, using *first*, *next* and *last*

materials: *Violet’s Life* on a screen, or the *Show your class* page (page 3)
questions: Violet was the second eldest girl in a big family. How did she help?
Why did Violet go to work when she was only 14?
What does a coat made small for a child tell us about Violet?
What would you like to ask Violet, if you could?
What keepsake would you choose for a woman in your family?
connection: **In the exhibition:** find Violet’s photographs on poster 2, and the family letters in the display case. **Online:** *Violet’s Life* asks a question at each stop, and *Make your own* sets out a timeline for a woman in your family.

steps.title: A thread of keepsakes
script: Show *Violet’s Life* (or page 3) without saying anything about it. *“A thread, with a little picture at each stop. Whose life could these pictures tell?”* Let children name the pictures: a house, a sewing machine, rings, a piano, a rose. *“Each picture is a keepsake: a small thing that helps us remember. Today they tell us about a real woman called Violet.”*

screen.alt: The Violet’s Life room: her places and moments along a line, above the first page of her story
screen.caption: Violet’s Life

steps.purpose: Wonder first: what can little pictures on a thread tell us?

steps.title: A girl in London
script: **A girl in London.** *“Violet was born in 1907 in London, a big city in England. She had three sisters and two brothers. She was the second eldest girl, so she helped look after her little sisters. At school she won certificates every year, and her teachers hoped she would become a teacher herself.”*

screen.alt: A sepia studio portrait of Violet as a young woman, standing beside a small pedestal table in a long belted coat with a strap across her chest, a brimmed hat and white gloves
screen.caption: Violet as a young woman

steps.purpose: Meet Violet as a girl: a big family, and a lot of helping.
students: How did Violet help at home?

steps.title: Work
script: **Work.** *“But when Violet was 14, one of her sisters needed to go to a special school, and the family needed money. So Violet left school and went to work in a factory, sewing at a machine. She was paid for every piece she finished.”* Play the sewing machine.

clips.label: A sewing machine

screen.question: This is the sound of Violet’s work. What do you think she made?

steps.purpose: Hear Violet’s work, and why a 14-year-old went to work.
students: Why did Violet go to work?

steps.title: A family of her own
script: **A family of her own.** *“Violet married Harold in 1928. She said she chose him because he made her laugh. They had two daughters and two sons. Money was often tight, but Violet was so good at sewing that she took grown-up coats apart and made them small for her children, so they were always warm.”*

items.caption: Out for a walk
items.alt: A sepia snapshot of three people walking arm in arm along a promenade: a woman holding a patterned parasol, a man in a straw hat and jacket, and a young woman in a pale blouse and dark trousers

items.caption: A family group
items.alt: A faded photograph of a family group outside a house: five women, three standing and two seated, with a baby in a white dress sitting between them

steps.purpose: See a family from long ago, and how Violet kept her children warm.
students: What do the photographs tell us?
How did Violet keep her children warm?

steps.title: Music and roses
script: **Music and roses.** *“Violet always had a piano. She played it by ear, and family and friends came to sing and dance at lively parties called knees-ups. Later, she had a house with a big garden, where she grew vegetables and flowers. Her favorite flowers were roses.”* Play the piano.

screen.question: A piano party, and a garden. Which would you like to visit?

steps.purpose: Hear the happy sounds of Violet’s home.

steps.title: First, next, last
script: Ask: *“Which came first in Violet’s life: the rose, the house or the sewing machine? Which came last?”* Children answer in a sentence: *“First, Violet lived in a house in London. Next, she worked at a sewing machine. Last, she grew roses.”*

screen.question: Which came first in Violet’s life: the rose, the house or the sewing machine? Which came last?

steps.purpose: Order three moments together before children do it alone.

steps.title: Choose a handout
script: Then children choose a handout. All three put Violet’s keepsakes in order and end with a keepsake of their own.

levels.name: Green Level
levels.summary: Number four keepsakes in order (the first is done), finish two sentences from a word box, and draw a keepsake for a woman in their family.

levels.name: Yellow Level
levels.summary: Number five keepsakes in order, retell Violet’s life with *first, next, last*, then draw a keepsake for a woman in their family and say why.

levels.name: Red Level
levels.summary: Number all six keepsakes, explain what the coat tells us about Violet, and write two questions for a woman in their own family.

steps.purpose: Put Violet’s life in order, at the right level of challenge.
students: Choose Green, Yellow or Red. All three put Violet’s keepsakes in order.

steps.title: Look back
script: Ask the objectives back from the screen: *“Can you now…?”* Children show a thumb up, sideways or down. Then: *“Think of a woman in your family. What would you ask her about when she was little? Tell a partner.”*
